rules.sentence: Individuals with deficiencies of any of the complement components, including proper-din, are highly susceptible to meningococcal infections.
Gram-negative bacilli cause meningitis in individuals with chronic and debilitating diseases such as diabetes, cirrhosis, or alcoholism and in those with chronic urinary tract infections.
Gram-negative meningitis can also complicate neurosurgical procedures, particularly craniotomy, and head trauma associated with CSF rhinorrhea or otorrhea.

Otitis, mastoiditis, and sinusitis are predisposing and associated conditions for meningitis due to Streptococci sp., gram-negative anaerobes, Staphylococcus aureus, Haemophilus sp., and Enterobacteriaceae.

Meningitis complicating endocarditis may be due to viridans streptococci, S. aureus, Streptococcus bovis, the HACEK group (Haemophilus sp., Actinobacillus actinomycetemcomitans, Cardiobacterium hominis, Eikenella corrodens, Kingella kingae), or enterococci.
